celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿الْحَمْدُ﴾ which is describing with what is beautiful, is established ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ the Exalted. Is the intent to inform of this so that it be believed, or to praise [Him] by it, or both? These are possibilities, the most informative of which is the third ﴿الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ عَلَى عَبْدِهِ﴾ Muhammad ﴿الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ﴾ i.e. in it ﴿عِوَجًا﴾ discrepancy or contradiction; and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الْكِتَابَ.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿قَيِّمًا﴾ straight; a second, emphatic ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ﴾ that He may warn the disbelievers with the Book of ﴿بَأْسًا﴾ a punishment ﴿شَدِيدًا مِنْ لَدُنْهُ﴾ from Allah ﴿وَيُبَشِّرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحَاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا حَسَنًا﴾

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَيُنْذِرَ﴾ from among the disbelievers ﴿الَّذِينَ قَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا﴾

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿مَا لَهُمْ بِهِ﴾ about this saying ﴿مِنْ عِلْمٍ وَلَا لِآبَائِهِمْ﴾ before them who said it ﴿كَبُرَتْ﴾ grievous is it ﴿كَلِمَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾ كَلِمَةً is a tamyīz (specification) explaining the vague pronoun, and the one specifically blamed (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. their aforementioned statement ﴿إِنْ﴾ not (إِنْ = مَا) ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ in that ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a statement ﴿كَذِبًا﴾

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿فَلَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ﴾ destroying ﴿نَفْسَكَ عَلَى آثَارِهِمْ﴾ after them, i.e. after they turn away from you ﴿إِنْ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِهَذَا الْحَدِيثِ﴾ the Quran ﴿أَسَفًا﴾ out of vexation and grief on your part, because of your eagerness for their faith; it is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose).

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا مَا عَلَى الْأَرْضِ﴾ of animals, plants, trees, rivers and other things ﴿زِينَةً لَهَا لِنَبْلُوَهُمْ﴾ that We may test people as they look at that ﴿أَيُّهُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا﴾ in it, i.e. most detached from it.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَإِنَّا لَجَاعِلُونَ مَا عَلَيْهَا صَعِيدًا﴾ crumbled dust ﴿جُرُزًا﴾ dry, growing nothing.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿أَمْ حَسِبْتَ﴾ i.e. did you think ﴿أَنَّ أَصْحَابَ الْكَهْفِ﴾ the cave in the mountain ﴿وَالرَّقِيمِ﴾ the tablet on which their names and lineages were written. He ﷺ had been asked about their story ﴿كَانُوا﴾ in their story ﴿مِنْ﴾ among ﴿آيَاتِنَا عَجَبًا﴾ the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ, and what precedes it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they were a wonder apart from the rest of the signs, or the most wondrous of them? The matter is not so. Remember:

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿إِذْ أَوَى الْفِتْيَةُ إِلَى الْكَهْفِ﴾ plural of فَتًى, which is the fully grown young man; fearing for their faith from their disbelieving people ﴿فَقَالُوا رَبَّنَا آتِنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ﴾ from You ﴿رَحْمَةً وَهَيِّئْ﴾ set right ﴿لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًا﴾ guidance.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿فَضَرَبْنَا عَلَى آذَانِهِمْ﴾ i.e. We made them sleep ﴿فِي الْكَهْفِ سِنِينَ عَدَدًا﴾ numbered.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَاهُمْ﴾ We woke them ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ﴾ with the knowledge of witnessing ﴿أَيُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ﴾ the two parties who differed about the length of their stay ﴿أَحْصَى﴾ the afʿal pattern meaning "more precise" ﴿لِمَا لَبِثُوا﴾ for their stay; attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows it ﴿أَمَدًا﴾ a term.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ﴾ We recite ﴿عَلَيْكَ نَبَأَهُمْ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ truthfully ﴿إِنَّهُمْ فِتْيَةٌ آمَنُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ وَزِدْنَاهُمْ هُدًى﴾

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَرَبَطْنَا عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ We strengthened them to speak the truth ﴿إِذْ قَامُوا﴾ before their king, when he had commanded them to prostrate to the idols ﴿فَقَالُوا رَبُّنَا رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَنْ نَدْعُوَ مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿إِلَهًا لَقَدْ قُلْنَا إِذًا شَطَطًا﴾ i.e. a saying of shaṭaṭ, i.e. of excess in disbelief, if, hypothetically, we called upon a god other than Allah.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿قَوْمُنَا﴾ ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) ﴿اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ آلِهَةً لَوْلَا﴾ why do they not ﴿يَأْتُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ for worshipping them ﴿بِسُلْطَانٍ بَيِّنٍ﴾ with a manifest proof ﴿فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ﴾ i.e. no one is more unjust ﴿مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ by ascribing a partner to Him, the Exalted. Some of the youths said to others:

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَإِذِ اعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ فَأْوُوا إِلَى الْكَهْفِ يَنْشُرْ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ مِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ وَيُهَيِّئْ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَمْرِكُمْ مِرْفَقًا﴾ with kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the fāʾ, and the reverse [مَرْفِقًا]: that by which you are sustained, of morning and evening meals.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَتَرَى الشَّمْسَ إِذَا طَلَعَتْ تَزَّاوَرُ﴾ with and without doubling [تَزَاوَرُ]: inclines ﴿عَنْ كَهْفِهِمْ ذَاتَ الْيَمِينِ﴾ its side ﴿وَإِذَا غَرَبَتْ تَقْرِضُهُمْ ذَاتَ الشِّمَالِ﴾ leaves them and passes them by, so it does not touch them at all ﴿وَهُمْ فِي فَجْوَةٍ مِنْهُ﴾ a wide space in the cave, where the coolness and breeze of the wind reach them ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ that has been mentioned ﴿مِنْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ the proofs of His power ﴿مَنْ يَهْدِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ وَلِيًّا مُرْشِدًا﴾

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَتَحْسَبُهُمْ﴾ if you saw them ﴿أَيْقَاظًا﴾ i.e. awake, because their eyes are open; plural of يَقِظ with kasra on the qāf ﴿وَهُمْ رُقُودٌ﴾ asleep; plural of رَاقِد ﴿وَنُقَلِّبُهُمْ ذَاتَ الْيَمِينِ وَذَاتَ الشِّمَالِ﴾ lest the earth consume their flesh ﴿وَكَلْبُهُمْ بَاسِطٌ ذِرَاعَيْهِ﴾ its forelegs ﴿بِالْوَصِيدِ﴾ at the threshold of the cave; whenever they turned over, it turned over like them, in sleep and in waking ﴿لَوِ اطَّلَعْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَوَلَّيْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِرَارًا وَلَمُلِّئْتَ﴾ with and without doubling [وَلَمُلِئْتَ] ﴿مِنْهُمْ رُعْبًا﴾ with sukūn and ḍamma on the ʿayn [رُعُبًا]. Allah protected them by terror from anyone entering upon them.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ just as We did with them what We mentioned ﴿بَعَثْنَاهُمْ﴾ We woke them ﴿لِيَتَسَاءَلُوا بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ about their state and the length of their stay ﴿قَالَ قَائِلٌ مِنْهُمْ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ قَالُوا لَبِثْنَا يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ﴾ because they entered the cave at sunrise and were woken at sunset, so they thought it was the sunset of the day they entered. Then ﴿قَالُوا﴾ hesitating about that ﴿رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا لَبِثْتُمْ فَابْعَثُوا أَحَدَكُمْ بِوَرِقِكُمْ﴾ with sukūn and kasra on the rāʾ [بِوَرْقِكُمْ]: with your silver ﴿هَذِهِ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ﴾ it is said that it is the one now called Ṭaraṭūs, with fatḥa on the rāʾ ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرْ أَيُّهَا أَزْكَى طَعَامًا﴾ which of the city's foods is most lawful ﴿فَلْيَأْتِكُمْ بِرِزْقٍ مِنْهُ وَلْيَتَلَطَّفْ وَلَا يُشْعِرَنَّ بِكُمْ أَحَدًا﴾

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ إِنْ يَظْهَرُوا عَلَيْكُمْ يَرْجُمُوكُمْ﴾ kill you by stoning ﴿أَوْ يُعِيدُوكُمْ فِي مِلَّتِهِمْ وَلَنْ تُفْلِحُوا إِذًا﴾ i.e. if you return to their religion ﴿أَبَدًا﴾

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ just as We woke them ﴿أَعْثَرْنَا﴾ We made aware ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ their people and the believers ﴿لِيَعْلَمُوا﴾ i.e. their people ﴿أَنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ of the resurrection ﴿حَقٌّ﴾ by way of [reasoning] that the One able to make them sleep for that long period and keep them in their state without food is able to bring the dead to life ﴿وَأَنَّ السَّاعَةَ لَا رَيْبَ﴾ no doubt ﴿فِيهَا إِذْ﴾ governed by (maʿmūl of) أَعْثَرْنَا ﴿يَتَنَازَعُونَ﴾ i.e. the believers and the disbelievers ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ أَمْرَهُمْ﴾ the matter of the youths, concerning building around them ﴿فَقَالُوا﴾ i.e. the disbelievers ﴿ابْنُوا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. around them ﴿بُنْيَانًا﴾ to conceal them ﴿رَبُّهُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِهِمْ قَالَ الَّذِينَ غَلَبُوا عَلَى أَمْرِهِمْ﴾ the matter of the youths, and they were the believers ﴿لَنَتَّخِذَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ around them ﴿مَسْجِدًا﴾ in which prayer is performed; and that was done at the entrance of the cave.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿سَيَقُولُونَ﴾ i.e. those disputing about the number of the youths in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, i.e. some of them will say: they are ﴿ثَلَاثَةٌ رَابِعُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ i.e. some of them ﴿خَمْسَةٌ سَادِسُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ﴾ and the two sayings belong to the Christians of Najrān ﴿رَجْمًا بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ i.e. guessing about them in their absence; it refers to both sayings together, and it is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. because of their guessing that ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ i.e. the believers ﴿سَبْعَةٌ وَثَامِنُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ﴾ the clause consisting of the mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate) is an adjective (ṣifa) of سَبْعَةٌ, with the wāw added; and it is said [the wāw is] for emphasis and indicates the adherence of the adjective to the noun it qualifies. Describing the first two [sayings] as guessing, but not the third, is evidence that it is approved and correct ﴿قُلْ رَبِّي أَعْلَمُ بِعِدَّتِهِمْ مَا يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ﴾ Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I am among the few", and he gave their number as seven ﴿فَلَا تُمَارِ﴾ do not dispute ﴿فِيهِمْ إِلَّا مِرَاءً ظَاهِرًا﴾ with what has been sent down to you ﴿وَلَا تَسْتَفْتِ فِيهِمْ﴾ seek a ruling ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ from the People of the Book, the Jews ﴿أَحَدًا﴾ The people of Mecca asked him about the story of the People of the Cave, and he said: "I will tell you about it tomorrow", without saying "if Allah wills"; so [the following] was revealed:

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿وَلَا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَيْءٍ﴾ i.e. concerning something ﴿إِنِّي فَاعِلٌ ذَلِكَ غَدًا﴾ i.e. in the time to come

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ i.e. except joined with the will of Allah the Exalted, by saying "if Allah wills" ﴿وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ﴾ i.e. His will, making [the matter] conditional on it ﴿إِذَا نَسِيتَ﴾ the making conditional on it; and mentioning it after forgetting is like mentioning it with the statement. Al-Ḥasan and others said: as long as he is still in the gathering ﴿وَقُلْ عَسَى أَنْ يَهْدِيَنِ رَبِّي لِأَقْرَبَ مِنْ هَذَا﴾ than the story of the People of the Cave, in proving my prophethood ﴿رَشَدًا﴾ guidance; and Allah did that.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَلَبِثُوا فِي كَهْفِهِمْ ثَلَاثَ مِائَةٍ﴾ with tanwīn ﴿سِنِينَ﴾ ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to ثَلَاثَمِائَةٍ. These three hundred years are solar according to the People of the Book, and the lunar ones, according to the Arabs, exceed them by nine years, which are mentioned in His saying: ﴿وَازْدَادُوا تِسْعًا﴾ i.e. nine years; so three hundred solar years are three hundred and nine lunar.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا لَبِثُوا﴾ than those who differed about it, and it is what has been mentioned above ﴿لَهُ غَيْبُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ i.e. the knowledge of it ﴿أَبْصِرْ بِهِ﴾ i.e. Allah; it is a form of exclamation (taʿajjub) ﴿وَأَسْمِعْ﴾ [with] Him likewise, in the meaning of "how seeing He is, and how hearing He is!" Both are by way of figurative usage (majāz), and the intent is that nothing is absent from His sight and hearing, the Exalted ﴿مَا لَهُمْ﴾ the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ﴾ a helper ﴿وَلَا يُشْرِكُ فِي حُكْمِهِ أَحَدًا﴾ because He has no need of a partner.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَاتْلُ مَا أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ كِتَابِ رَبِّكَ لَا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِمَاتِهِ وَلَنْ تَجِدَ مِنْ دُونِهِ مُلْتَحَدًا﴾ a refuge.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿وَاصْبِرْ نَفْسَكَ﴾ restrain it ﴿مَعَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ﴾ by their worship ﴿وَجْهَهُ﴾ the Exalted's, not any worldly aim; they are the poor ﴿وَلَا تَعْدُ﴾ turn away ﴿عَيْنَاكَ عَنْهُمْ﴾ by them [the two eyes] their owner is meant ﴿تُرِيدُ زِينَةَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَلَا تُطِعْ مَنْ أَغْفَلْنَا قَلْبَهُ عَنْ ذِكْرِنَا﴾ i.e. the Quran; he is ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn and his companions ﴿وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ﴾ in idolatry ﴿وَكَانَ أَمْرُهُ فُرُطًا﴾ excess.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَقُلِ﴾ to him and his companions: this Quran is ﴿الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَمَنْ شَاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِنْ وَمَنْ شَاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ﴾ a threat to them ﴿إِنَّا أَعْتَدْنَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers ﴿نَارًا أَحَاطَ بِهِمْ سُرَادِقُهَا﴾ what surrounds it ﴿وَإِنْ يَسْتَغِيثُوا يُغَاثُوا بِمَاءٍ كَالْمُهْلِ﴾ like the dregs of oil ﴿يَشْوِي الْوُجُوهَ﴾ from its heat when brought near them ﴿بِئْسَ الشَّرَابُ﴾ it is ﴿وَسَاءَتْ﴾ i.e. the Fire ﴿مُرْتَفَقًا﴾ a tamyīz (specification) transferred from the fāʿil (agent), i.e. its resting place is evil; it is set against His coming saying about Paradise وَحَسُنَتْ مُرْتَفَقًا, otherwise what resting is there in the Fire?

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ إِنَّا لَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ مَنْ أَحْسَنَ عَمَلًا﴾ The clause is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ الَّذِينَ, and in it the overt noun stands in place of the pronoun; the meaning is "their reward", i.e. We reward them with what it implies.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ﴾ of abiding ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمُ الْأَنْهَارُ يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيهَا مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ﴾ it is said that مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida), and it is said it is partitive; it [أَسَاوِر] is the plural of أَسْوِرَة, like أَحْمِرَة, the plural of سِوَار ﴿مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَيَلْبَسُونَ ثِيَابًا خُضْرًا مِنْ سُنْدُسٍ﴾ the fine kind of brocade ﴿وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ﴾ the thick kind of it; and in the verse of [Sūrat] al-Raḥmān: بَطَائِنُهَا مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ﴾ plural of أَرِيكَة, which is the couch in the ḥajala, a chamber adorned with cloths and curtains for the bride ﴿نِعْمَ الثَّوَابُ﴾ the recompense, Paradise ﴿وَحَسُنَتْ مُرْتَفَقًا﴾

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَاضْرِبْ﴾ set forth ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ for the disbelievers together with the believers ﴿مَثَلًا رَجُلَيْنِ﴾ a badal (substitute); it and what follows it are an explanation of the similitude ﴿جَعَلْنَا لِأَحَدِهِمَا﴾ the disbeliever ﴿جَنَّتَيْنِ﴾ two gardens ﴿مِنْ أَعْنَابٍ وَحَفَفْنَاهُمَا بِنَخْلٍ وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُمَا زَرْعًا﴾ for sustenance.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿كِلْتَا الْجَنَّتَيْنِ﴾ كِلْتَا is singular [in form] indicating duality; mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿آتَتْ﴾ its khabar (predicate) ﴿أُكُلَهَا﴾ its fruit ﴿وَلَمْ تَظْلِمْ﴾ diminish ﴿مِنْهُ شَيْئًا وَفَجَّرْنَا﴾ i.e. We cleaved ﴿خِلَالَهُمَا نَهَرًا﴾ flowing between them.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَكَانَ لَهُ﴾ besides the two gardens ﴿ثَمَرٌ﴾ with fatḥa on the thāʾ and the mīm, with ḍamma on both [ثُمُرٌ], and with ḍamma on the first and sukūn on the second [ثُمْرٌ]; it is the plural of ثَمَرَة, like شَجَرَة and شَجَر, خَشَبَة and خُشُب, بَدَنَة and بُدْن ﴿فَقَالَ لِصَاحِبِهِ﴾ the believer ﴿وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُ﴾ vying in boasting with him ﴿أَنَا أَكْثَرُ مِنْكَ مَالًا وَأَعَزُّ نَفَرًا﴾ in kinsfolk.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿وَدَخَلَ جَنَّتَهُ﴾ with his companion, taking him around in it and showing him its fruits. He did not say "his two gardens", meaning the garden [as a whole]; and it is said: being content with the singular ﴿وَهُوَ ظَالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ﴾ by disbelief ﴿قَالَ مَا أَظُنُّ أَنْ تَبِيدَ﴾ will cease to exist ﴿هَذِهِ أَبَدًا﴾

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَمَا أَظُنُّ السَّاعَةَ قَائِمَةً وَلَئِنْ رُدِدْتُ إِلَى رَبِّي﴾ in the Hereafter, as you claim ﴿لَأَجِدَنَّ خَيْرًا مِنْهَا مُنْقَلَبًا﴾ as a place of return.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿قَالَ لَهُ صَاحِبُهُ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُ﴾ answering him ﴿أَكَفَرْتَ بِالَّذِي خَلَقَكَ مِنْ تُرَابٍ﴾ because Adam was created from it ﴿ثُمَّ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ﴾ semen ﴿ثُمَّ سَوَّاكَ﴾ proportioned you and made you ﴿رَجُلًا﴾

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿لَكِنَّا﴾ its origin is لَكِنْ أَنَا; the vowel of the hamza was transferred to the nūn, or the hamza was dropped, then the nūn was assimilated into its like ﴿هُوَ﴾ the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), explained by the clause after it; the meaning is: I say ﴿اللَّهُ رَبِّي وَلَا أُشْرِكُ بِرَبِّي أَحَدًا﴾

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿وَلَوْلَا﴾ why did you not ﴿إِذْ دَخَلْتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلْتَ﴾ when you admired it, this: ﴿مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ﴾ And in the hadith: "Whoever is given some good, of wealth or family, and says at that: 'What Allah wills; there is no power except in Allah', will see nothing disliked in it." ﴿إِنْ تَرَنِ أَنَا﴾ a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) between the two objects ﴿أَقَلَّ مِنْكَ مَالًا وَوَلَدًا﴾

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿فَعَسَى رَبِّي أَنْ يُؤْتِيَنِ خَيْرًا مِنْ جَنَّتِكَ﴾ the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) ﴿وَيُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهَا حُسْبَانًا﴾ plural of حُسْبَانَة, i.e. thunderbolts ﴿مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَتُصْبِحَ صَعِيدًا زَلَقًا﴾ smooth ground on which no foot stays firm.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿أَوْ يُصْبِحَ مَاؤُهَا غَوْرًا﴾ meaning sunk; conjoined to يُرْسِلَ, not to تُصْبِحَ, because the sinking of the water is not caused by the thunderbolts ﴿فَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعَ لَهُ طَلَبًا﴾ a means by which you could reach it.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿وَأُحِيطَ بِثَمَرِهِ﴾ with the vocalisations mentioned earlier; together with his garden, by destruction, so it perished ﴿فَأَصْبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ﴾ in regret and sorrow ﴿عَلَى مَا أَنْفَقَ فِيهَا﴾ on cultivating his garden ﴿وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ﴾ fallen down ﴿عَلَى عُرُوشِهَا﴾ its supports for the vines, in that they fell and then the vines fell ﴿وَيَقُولُ يَا﴾ for calling attention ﴿لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُشْرِكْ بِرَبِّي أَحَدًا﴾

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿وَلَمْ تَكُنْ﴾ with tāʾ and yāʾ [يَكُنْ] ﴿لَهُ فِئَةٌ﴾ a group ﴿يَنْصُرُونَهُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ at its destruction ﴿وَمَا كَانَ مُنْتَصِرًا﴾ by himself at its destruction.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿هُنَالِكَ﴾ i.e. on the Day of Resurrection ﴿الْوَلَايَةُ﴾ with fatḥa on the wāw: support; with kasra [الْوِلَايَةُ]: dominion ﴿لِلَّهِ الْحَقُّ﴾ in the nominative, an adjective (ṣifa) of الْوَلَايَةُ; and in the genitive, an adjective of the Majestic Name [الْحَقِّ] ﴿هُوَ خَيْرٌ ثَوَابًا﴾ than the reward of any other, if [another] could reward ﴿وَخَيْرٌ عُقْبًا﴾ with ḍamma and sukūn on the qāf [عُقُبًا]: as an outcome for the believers; both are accusative as tamyīz (specification).

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿وَاضْرِبْ﴾ make ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ for your people ﴿مَثَلَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ first object ﴿كَمَاءٍ﴾ second object ﴿أَنْزَلْنَاهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَاخْتَلَطَ بِهِ﴾ became dense because of the coming down of the water ﴿نَبَاتُ الْأَرْضِ﴾ or the water mingled with the plants, so they were watered and flourished ﴿فَأَصْبَحَ﴾ the plants became ﴿هَشِيمًا﴾ dry, its parts scattered ﴿تَذْرُوهُ﴾ scatter and disperse it ﴿الرِّيَاحُ﴾ and carry it away. The meaning: He likened the world to beautiful vegetation that dried, broke, and was scattered by the winds. In one reading: [الرِّيحُ] ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُقْتَدِرًا﴾ able.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿الْمَالُ وَالْبَنُونَ زِينَةُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ one adorns oneself with them in it ﴿وَالْبَاقِيَاتُ الصَّالِحَاتُ﴾ they are: "Glory be to Allah", "Praise be to Allah", "There is no god but Allah" and "Allah is greatest"; some added: "There is no might nor power except in Allah" ﴿خَيْرٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَابًا وَخَيْرٌ أَمَلًا﴾ i.e. what a person hopes and expects with Allah the Exalted.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿يَوْمَ تُسَيِّرُ الْجِبَالَ﴾ they are removed from the face of the earth and become scattered dust; in one reading with nūn, kasra on the yāʾ and the accusative of الْجِبَال [نُسَيِّرُ الْجِبَالَ] ﴿وَتَرَى الْأَرْضَ بَارِزَةً﴾ exposed, with nothing on it, neither mountain nor anything else ﴿وَحَشَرْنَاهُمْ﴾ the believers and the disbelievers ﴿فَلَمْ نُغَادِرْ﴾ leave ﴿مِنْهُمْ أَحَدًا﴾

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَعُرِضُوا عَلَى رَبِّكَ صَفًّا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. standing in rows, each community a row, and it will be said to them: ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾ i.e. alone, barefoot, naked and uncircumcised; and it will be said to the deniers of the resurrection: ﴿بَلْ زَعَمْتُمْ أَ﴾نْ lightened from the heavy [أَنَّ], i.e. أَنَّهُ ﴿لَنْ نَجْعَلَ لَكُمْ مَوْعِدًا﴾ for the resurrection.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿وَوُضِعَ الْكِتَابُ﴾ the record of every person: in the right hand of the believers and in the left hand of the disbelievers ﴿فَتَرَى الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers ﴿مُشْفِقِينَ﴾ fearful ﴿مِمَّا فِيهِ وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ upon seeing the evil deeds in it ﴿يَا﴾ for calling attention ﴿وَيْلَتَنَا﴾ our destruction; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that has no verb from its root ﴿مَالِ هَذَا الْكِتَابِ لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةً وَلَا كَبِيرَةً﴾ of our sins ﴿إِلَّا أَحْصَاهَا﴾ counted and recorded it; they marvelled at it in that ﴿وَوَجَدُوا مَا عَمِلُوا حَاضِرًا﴾ recorded in their book ﴿وَلَا يَظْلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَدًا﴾ He does not punish him without a crime, nor diminish the reward of a believer.

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿وَإِذْ﴾ accusative by [an implied] "remember" ﴿قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ﴾ a prostration of bowing, not placing the forehead [on the ground], as a greeting to him ﴿فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ كَانَ مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ it is said they are a kind of angel, so the exception is connected (muttaṣil); and it is said it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), Iblīs being the father of the jinn, so he has offspring, mentioned with him later, whereas the angels have no offspring ﴿فَفَسَقَ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِ﴾ i.e. he departed from His obedience by refusing to prostrate ﴿أَفَتَتَّخِذُونَهُ وَذُرِّيَّتَهُ﴾ the address is to Adam and his offspring, and the hāʾ in both places refers to Iblīs ﴿أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِي﴾ obeying them ﴿وَهُمْ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ﴾ i.e. enemies ﴿بِئْسَ لِلظَّالِمِينَ بَدَلًا﴾ Iblīs and his offspring, in obeying them instead of obeying Allah.

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿مَا أَشْهَدْتُهُمْ﴾ i.e. Iblīs and his offspring ﴿خَلْقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَلَا خَلْقَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ i.e. I did not make some of them present at the creation of others ﴿وَمَا كُنْتُ مُتَّخِذَ الْمُضِلِّينَ﴾ the devils ﴿عَضُدًا﴾ helpers in creation; so how can you obey them?

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾ accusative by [an implied] "remember" ﴿يَقُولُ﴾ with yāʾ and nūn [نَقُولُ] ﴿نَادُوا شُرَكَائِي﴾ the idols ﴿الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ﴾ would intercede for you, as you claimed ﴿فَدَعَوْهُمْ فَلَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَهُمْ﴾ did not answer them ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ between the idols and their worshippers ﴿مَوْبِقًا﴾ a valley among the valleys of Hell in which they all perish; it is from وَبَقَ, with fatḥa: he perished.

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿وَرَأَى الْمُجْرِمُونَ النَّارَ فَظَنُّوا﴾ i.e. were certain ﴿أَنَّهُمْ مُوَاقِعُوهَا﴾ i.e. falling into it ﴿وَلَمْ يَجِدُوا عَنْهَا مَصْرِفًا﴾ a way of escape.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَا﴾ We have set forth clearly ﴿فِي هَذَا الْقُرْآنِ لِلنَّاسِ مِنْ كُلِّ مَثَلٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted noun, i.e. "a similitude of the kind of every similitude", so that they may take admonition ﴿وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ﴾ i.e. the disbeliever ﴿أَكْثَرَ شَيْءٍ جَدَلًا﴾ contention in falsehood; it is a tamyīz (specification) transferred from the noun of كَانَ; the meaning is: man's contentiousness is the most abundant thing in him.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿وَمَا مَنَعَ النَّاسَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca ﴿أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا﴾ second object ﴿إِذْ جَاءَهُمُ الْهُدَى﴾ the Quran ﴿وَيَسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ سُنَّةُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ fāʿil (agent), i.e. Our way with them, which is the destruction decreed for them ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ الْعَذَابُ قِبَلًا﴾ face to face and openly, and that is the killing on the day of Badr; in one reading with two ḍammas, plural of قَبِيل [قُبُلًا], i.e. in various kinds.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿وَمَا نُرْسِلُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرِينَ﴾ to the believers ﴿وَمُنْذِرِينَ﴾ warning the disbelievers ﴿وَيُجَادِلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِالْبَاطِلِ﴾ by their saying "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?" and the like ﴿لِيُدْحِضُوا بِهِ﴾ to nullify by their disputing ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَاتَّخَذُوا آيَاتِي﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿وَمَا أُنْذِرُوا﴾ with it, of the Fire ﴿هُزُوًا﴾ an object of ridicule.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ ذُكِّرَ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِ فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهَا وَنَسِيَ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ﴾ the disbelief and sins he committed ﴿إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً﴾ coverings ﴿أَنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ﴾ i.e. [preventing them] from understanding the Quran, i.e. so they do not understand it ﴿وَفِي آذَانِهِمْ وَقْرًا﴾ heaviness, so they do not hear it ﴿وَإِنْ تَدْعُهُمْ إِلَى الْهُدَى فَلَنْ يَهْتَدُوا إِذًا﴾ i.e. given the making mentioned ﴿أَبَدًا﴾

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿وَرَبُّكَ الْغَفُورُ ذُو الرَّحْمَةِ لَوْ يُؤَاخِذُهُمْ﴾ in this world ﴿بِمَا كَسَبُوا لَعَجَّلَ لَهُمُ الْعَذَابَ﴾ in it ﴿بَلْ لَهُمْ مَوْعِدٌ﴾ and that is the Day of Resurrection ﴿لَنْ يَجِدُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ مَوْئِلًا﴾ a refuge.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿وَتِلْكَ الْقُرَى﴾ i.e. their people, such as ʿĀd, Thamūd and others ﴿أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ لَمَّا ظَلَمُوا﴾ disbelieved ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا لِمُهْلَكِهِمْ﴾ for their destruction; in one reading with fatḥa on the mīm [لِمَهْلِكِهِمْ], i.e. for their perishing ﴿مَوْعِدًا﴾

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ قَالَ مُوسَى﴾ he is the son of ʿImrān ﴿لِفَتَاهُ﴾ Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn, who used to follow him, serve him and take knowledge from him ﴿لَا أَبْرَحُ﴾ I will keep travelling ﴿حَتَّى أَبْلُغَ مَجْمَعَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ﴾ the meeting point of the Sea of the Romans and the Sea of Persia, on the side towards the east, i.e. the place joining them ﴿أَوْ أَمْضِيَ حُقُبًا﴾ a long time in reaching it, if it is far.

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا بَلَغَا مَجْمَعَ بَيْنِهِمَا﴾ between the two seas ﴿نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا﴾ Yūshaʿ forgot to carry it when setting off, and Moses forgot to remind him ﴿فَاتَّخَذَ﴾ the fish ﴿سَبِيلَهُ فِي الْبَحْرِ﴾ i.e. made it, by Allah's making ﴿سَرَبًا﴾ i.e. like a tunnel, which is a long cleft with no outlet. That was because Allah the Exalted held back the flow of the water from the fish, so it parted from it and remained like an opening that did not close, and the water beneath it became solid.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَا﴾ that place, travelling until the time of the morning meal on the second day ﴿قَالَ﴾ Moses ﴿لِفَتَاهُ آتِنَا غَدَاءَنَا﴾ it is what is eaten at the beginning of the day ﴿لَقَدْ لَقِينَا مِنْ سَفَرِنَا هَذَا نَصَبًا﴾ fatigue; and it came about after passing [the place].

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿قَالَ أَرَأَيْتَ﴾ i.e. take note ﴿إِذْ أَوَيْنَا إِلَى الصَّخْرَةِ﴾ in that place ﴿فَإِنِّي نَسِيتُ الْحُوتَ وَمَا أَنْسَانِيهُ إِلَّا الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ substituted for the hāʾ is ﴿أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُ﴾ a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion), i.e. he made me forget to mention it ﴿وَاتَّخَذَ﴾ the fish ﴿سَبِيلَهُ فِي الْبَحْرِ عَجَبًا﴾ second object, i.e. Moses and his young man marvelled at it, for the reason given in its explanation above.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Moses ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. our losing the fish ﴿مَا﴾ i.e. that which ﴿كُنَّا نَبْغِ﴾ we were seeking, for it is a sign for us of the presence of the one we seek ﴿فَارْتَدَّا﴾ they went back ﴿عَلَى آثَارِهِمَا﴾ retracing them ﴿قَصَصًا﴾ and they came to the rock.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿فَوَجَدَا عَبْدًا مِنْ عِبَادِنَا﴾ he is al-Khaḍir ﴿آتَيْنَاهُ رَحْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِنَا﴾ prophethood according to one view, and sainthood (walāya) according to another, which most scholars hold ﴿وَعَلَّمْنَاهُ مِنْ لَدُنَّا﴾ from Us ﴿عِلْمًا﴾ second object, i.e. something known of the unseen matters. Al-Bukhārī narrated the hadith that Moses stood to preach among the Children of Israel and was asked: "Which of the people is most knowledgeable?" He said: "I." So Allah reproached him, since he had not referred the knowledge to Him, and Allah revealed to him: "I have a servant at the meeting of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you." Moses said: "O Lord, how can I reach him?" He said: "Take a fish with you and put it in a basket; wherever you lose the fish, he is there." So he took a fish, put it in a basket, then set out, and his young man Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn set out with him, until they came to the rock and laid down their heads and slept. The fish stirred in the basket, came out of it and fell into the sea, ﴿فَاتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ فِي الْبَحْرِ سَرَبًا﴾, and Allah held back the flow of the water from the fish, so that it became like an arch over it. When he woke up, his companion forgot to tell him about the fish, so they travelled the rest of their day and their night, until, when it was morning, Moses said to his young man: ﴿آتِنَا غَدَاءَنَا﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَاتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ فِي الْبَحْرِ عَجَبًا﴾. He said: For the fish it was a tunnel, and for Moses and his young man a wonder … etc.

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿قَالَ لَهُ مُوسَى هَلْ أَتَّبِعُكَ عَلَى أَنْ تُعَلِّمَنِ مِمَّا عُلِّمْتَ رَشَدًا﴾ i.e. what is right, by which I may be guided; in one reading with ḍamma on the rāʾ and sukūn on the shīn [رُشْدًا]. He asked him that because increase in knowledge is something to be sought.

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّكَ لَنْ تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِيَ صَبْرًا﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿وَكَيْفَ تَصْبِرُ عَلَى مَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ خُبْرًا﴾ In the previous hadith, following this verse: "O Moses, I have knowledge from Allah which He taught me and which you do not know, and you have knowledge from Allah which Allah taught you and which I do not know." His saying خُبْرًا is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the meaning of لَمْ تُحِطْ, i.e. you have not experienced its reality.

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿قَالَ سَتَجِدُنِي إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ صَابِرًا وَلَا أَعْصِي﴾ i.e. and not disobeying ﴿لَكَ أَمْرًا﴾ which you command me. He made it conditional on [Allah's] will because he was not confident of himself in what he undertook; and this is the custom of the prophets and the saints: not to rely on themselves for the blink of an eye.

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿قَالَ فَإِنِ اتَّبَعْتَنِي فَلَا تَسْأَلْنِي﴾ in one reading with fatḥa on the lām and doubling of the nūn [تَسْأَلَنِّي] ﴿عَنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ that you find objectionable in me according to your knowledge, and be patient ﴿حَتَّى أُحْدِثَ لَكَ مِنْهُ ذِكْرًا﴾ i.e. I mention it to you with its reason. So Moses accepted his condition, observing the etiquette of the learner with the scholar.

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿فَانْطَلَقَا﴾ walking along the seashore ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا رَكِبَا فِي السَّفِينَةِ﴾ which passed by them ﴿خَرَقَهَا﴾ al-Khaḍir, by pulling out one or two planks from it on the sea side with an axe, when it reached the deep water ﴿قَالَ﴾ Moses to him ﴿أَخَرَقْتَهَا لِتُغْرِقَ أَهْلَهَا﴾ in one reading with fatḥa on the lower-dotted letter [yāʾ] and on the rāʾ, and the nominative of أَهْلُهَا [لِيَغْرَقَ أَهْلُهَا] ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئًا إِمْرًا﴾ i.e. something grave and objectionable. It is narrated that the water did not enter it.

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ إِنَّكَ لَنْ تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِيَ صَبْرًا﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿قَالَ لَا تُؤَاخِذْنِي بِمَا نَسِيتُ﴾ i.e. I was heedless of submitting to you and refraining from objecting to you ﴿وَلَا تُرْهِقْنِي﴾ burden me ﴿مِنْ أَمْرِي عُسْرًا﴾ with hardship in my keeping company with you, i.e. treat me in it with pardon and ease.

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿فَانْطَلَقَا﴾ after leaving the ship, walking ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا لَقِيَا غُلَامًا﴾ who had not reached puberty, playing with the boys, the most handsome of them in face ﴿فَقَتَلَهُ﴾ al-Khaḍir, by slaughtering him with a knife while he lay down, or by tearing off his head with his hand, or by striking his head against a wall; [these are differing] views. Here the conjoining fāʾ is used because the killing followed the meeting; and the apodosis of إِذَا is ﴿قَالَ﴾ Moses to him ﴿أَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا زَاكِيَةً﴾ i.e. pure, not having reached the age of legal responsibility; in one reading [زَكِيَّةً], with doubled yāʾ and no alif ﴿بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ﴾ i.e. it had not killed a soul ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئًا نُكْرًا﴾ with sukūn and ḍamma on the kāf [نُكُرًا], i.e. objectionable.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَكَ إِنَّكَ لَنْ تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِيَ صَبْرًا﴾ He added لَكَ compared with the previous [statement] because there was no excuse here; and for this reason:

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿قَالَ إِنْ سَأَلْتُكَ عَنْ شَيْءٍ بَعْدَهَا﴾ i.e. after this time ﴿فَلَا تُصَاحِبْنِي﴾ do not let me follow you ﴿قَدْ بَلَغْتَ مِنْ لَدُنِّي﴾ with doubling and without [لَدُنِي]: from me ﴿عُذْرًا﴾ for your parting from me.

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿فَانْطَلَقَا حَتَّى إِذَا أَتَيَا أَهْلَ قَرْيَةٍ﴾ it is Antioch ﴿اسْتَطْعَمَا أَهْلَهَا﴾ they asked them for food as hospitality ﴿فَأَبَوْا أَنْ يُضَيِّفُوهُمَا فَوَجَدَا فِيهَا جِدَارًا﴾ a hundred cubits high ﴿يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَنْقَضَّ﴾ i.e. was about to fall because of its leaning ﴿فَأَقَامَهُ﴾ al-Khaḍir, with his hand ﴿قَالَ﴾ Moses to him ﴿لَوْ شِئْتَ لَتَخِذْتَ﴾ in one reading [لَاتَّخَذْتَ] ﴿عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًا﴾ a payment, since they did not host us although we were in need of food.

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ al-Khaḍir to him ﴿هَذَا فِرَاقُ﴾ i.e. the time of parting ﴿بَيْنِي وَبَيْنِكَ﴾ Here بَيْن is annexed to something not plural, which is permitted by its repetition through conjunction with wāw ﴿سَأُنَبِّئُكَ﴾ before I part from you ﴿بِتَأْوِيلِ مَا لَمْ تَسْتَطِعْ عَلَيْهِ صَبْرًا﴾

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿أَمَّا السَّفِينَةُ فَكَانَتْ لِمَسَاكِينَ﴾ ten ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ فِي الْبَحْرِ﴾ with it, hiring it out to earn a living ﴿فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَعِيبَهَا وَكَانَ وَرَاءَهُمْ﴾ when they returned, or [it means] before them now ﴿مَلِكٌ﴾ a disbeliever ﴿يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ﴾ sound ﴿غَصْبًا﴾ accusative as a maṣdar specifying the kind of taking.

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا الْغُلَامُ فَكَانَ أَبَوَاهُ مُؤْمِنَيْنِ فَخَشِينَا أَنْ يُرْهِقَهُمَا طُغْيَانًا وَكُفْرًا﴾ for he, as in the hadith of Muslim, was created [with a nature] disposed to disbelief, and had he lived he would have burdened them with that, because out of their love for him they would follow him in it.

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿فَأَرَدْنَا أَنْ يُبَدِّلَهُمَا﴾ with and without doubling [يُبْدِلَهُمَا] ﴿رَبُّهُمَا خَيْرًا مِنْهُ زَكَوةً﴾ i.e. in righteousness and piety ﴿وَأَقْرَبَ﴾ than him ﴿رُحْمًا﴾ with sukūn and ḍamma on the ḥāʾ [رُحُمًا]: mercy, which is dutifulness to his parents. So Allah the Exalted gave them in exchange a girl who married a prophet and bore a prophet, through whom Allah the Exalted guided a nation.

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا الْجِدَارُ فَكَانَ لِغُلَامَيْنِ يَتِيمَيْنِ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ وَكَانَ تَحْتَهُ كَنْزٌ﴾ buried wealth of gold and silver ﴿لَهُمَا وَكَانَ أَبُوهُمَا صَالِحًا﴾ so they were preserved through his righteousness, in their persons and their wealth ﴿فَأَرَادَ رَبُّكَ أَنْ يَبْلُغَا أَشُدَّهُمَا﴾ i.e. the perceiving of their maturity ﴿وَيَسْتَخْرِجَا كَنْزَهُمَا رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), governed by أَرَادَ ﴿وَمَا فَعَلْتُهُ﴾ i.e. what was mentioned: making a hole in the ship, killing the boy and setting up the wall ﴿عَنْ أَمْرِي﴾ i.e. my own choice, but by the command of inspiration from Allah ﴿ذَلِكَ تَأْوِيلُ مَا لَمْ تَسْطِعْ عَلَيْهِ صَبْرًا﴾ One says اسْطَاعَ and اسْتَطَاعَ in the meaning of "was able"; so in this and what precedes it the two usages are combined. And the expression was varied in فَأَرَدْتُ, فَأَرَدْنَا and فَأَرَادَ رَبُّكَ.

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ﴾ i.e. the Jews ﴿عَنْ ذِي الْقَرْنَيْنِ﴾ his name was al-Iskandar, and he was not a prophet ﴿قُلْ سَأَتْلُوا﴾ I will relate ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْهُ﴾ of his state ﴿ذِكْرًا﴾ an account.

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿إِنَّا مَكَّنَّا لَهُ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ by making travel in it easy ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ he needed ﴿سَبَبًا﴾ a way leading him to his aim.

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿فَأَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا﴾ he took a way towards the west.

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا بَلَغَ مَغْرِبَ الشَّمْسِ﴾ the place of its setting ﴿وَجَدَهَا تَغْرُبُ فِي عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍ﴾ having ḥamaʾ, which is black mud; its setting in the spring is as it appears to the eye, for otherwise it is greater than the world ﴿وَوَجَدَ عِنْدَهَا﴾ i.e. the spring ﴿قَوْمًا﴾ disbelieving ﴿قُلْنَا يَا ذَا الْقَرْنَيْنِ﴾ by inspiration ﴿إِمَّا أَنْ تُعَذِّبَ﴾ the people, by killing ﴿وَإِمَّا أَنْ تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًا﴾ by taking captive.

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿قَالَ أَمَّا مَنْ ظَلَمَ﴾ by idolatry ﴿فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُ﴾ we will kill him ﴿ثُمَّ يُرَدُّ إِلَى رَبِّهِ فَيُعَذِّبُهُ عَذَابًا نُكْرًا﴾ with sukūn and ḍamma on the kāf [نُكُرًا]: severe, in the Fire.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا مَنْ آمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَلَهُ جَزَاءُ الْحُسْنَى﴾ i.e. Paradise, and the annexation (iḍāfa) is explicative; in one reading with جَزَاءً in the accusative with tanwīn. Al-Farrāʾ said: its accusative is by way of explanation (tafsīr), i.e. with respect to the attribution ﴿وَسَنَقُولُ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِنَا يُسْرًا﴾ i.e. we will command him with what is easy for him.

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا بَلَغَ مَطْلِعَ الشَّمْسِ﴾ the place of its rising ﴿وَجَدَهَا تَطْلُعُ عَلَى قَوْمٍ﴾ they are the Zanj ﴿لَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِهَا﴾ i.e. the sun ﴿سِتْرًا﴾ of clothing or roof, because their land does not bear buildings; they have tunnels in which they disappear when the sun rises, and they come out when it is high.

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the matter is as We have said ﴿وَقَدْ أَحَطْنَا بِمَا لَدَيْهِ﴾ i.e. with Dhū al-Qarnayn, of equipment, troops and other things ﴿خُبْرًا﴾ in knowledge.

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا بَلَغَ بَيْنَ السَّدَّيْنِ﴾ with fatḥa and ḍamma on the sīn [السُّدَّيْنِ], here and in the two after it: two mountains at the far end of the land of the Turks, the space between which al-Iskandar walled off, as will come ﴿وَجَدَ مِنْ دُونِهِمَا﴾ i.e. in front of them ﴿قَوْمًا لَا يَكَادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ قَوْلًا﴾ i.e. they do not understand it except slowly; in one reading with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the qāf [يُفْقِهُونَ].

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿قَالُوا يَا ذَا الْقَرْنَيْنِ إِنَّ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ﴾ with and without hamza; they are two foreign names of two tribes, and so they are diptotes ﴿مُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ by plunder and wrongdoing when they come out against us ﴿فَهَلْ نَجْعَلُ لَكَ خَرْجًا﴾ a payment of money; in one reading [خَرَاجًا] ﴿عَلَى أَنْ تَجْعَلَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُمْ سَدًّا﴾ a barrier, so that they do not reach us.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿قَالَ مَا مَكَّنِّي﴾ in one reading with two nūns without assimilation [مَكَّنَنِي] ﴿فِيهِ رَبِّي﴾ of wealth and other things ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ than your payment which you would give me, so I have no need of it, and I will make the barrier for you voluntarily ﴿فَأَعِينُونِي بِقُوَّةٍ﴾ for what I ask of you ﴿أَجْعَلْ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ رَدْمًا﴾ a fortified barrier.

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿آتُونِي زُبَرَ الْحَدِيدِ﴾ pieces the size of the stones used for building; so he built with them and placed firewood and charcoal between them ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا سَاوَى بَيْنَ الصُّدُفَيْنِ﴾ with ḍamma on both letters, with fatḥa on both [الصَّدَفَيْنِ], and with ḍamma on the first and sukūn on the second [الصُّدْفَيْنِ]: i.e. the two sides of the two mountains, with the building; and he placed the bellows and the fire around that ﴿قَالَ انْفُخُوا﴾ so they blew ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا جَعَلَهُ﴾ i.e. the iron ﴿نَارًا﴾ i.e. like fire ﴿قَالَ آتُونِي أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْرًا﴾ it is molten copper. The two verbs contend for it (tanāzuʿ), and it was omitted from the first because the second was made to govern. So he poured the molten copper over the heated iron, and it entered between its pieces and they became one thing.

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿فَمَا اسْطَاعُوا﴾ i.e. Gog and Magog ﴿أَنْ يَظْهَرُوهُ﴾ to climb on top of it, because of its height and smoothness ﴿وَمَا اسْتَطَاعُوا لَهُ نَقْبًا﴾ piercing, because of its hardness and thickness.

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Dhū al-Qarnayn ﴿هَذَا﴾ i.e. the barrier, i.e. the ability to make it ﴿رَحْمَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّي﴾ a favour, because it prevents their coming out ﴿فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَعْدُ رَبِّي﴾ of their coming out near the resurrection ﴿جَعَلَهُ دَكَّاءَ﴾ levelled and flattened ﴿وَكَانَ وَعْدُ رَبِّي﴾ of their coming out and other things ﴿حَقًّا﴾ bound to happen.

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿وَتَرَكْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ the day of their coming out ﴿يَمُوجُ فِي بَعْضٍ﴾ mingling with one another because of their great number ﴿وَنُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ﴾ i.e. the horn, for the resurrection ﴿فَجَمَعْنَاهُمْ﴾ i.e. the creatures, in one place on the Day of Resurrection ﴿جَمْعًا﴾

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿وَعَرَضْنَا﴾ We brought near ﴿جَهَنَّمَ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَرْضًا﴾

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَانَتْ أَعْيُنُهُمْ﴾ a badal (substitute) for الْكَافِرِينَ ﴿فِي غِطَاءٍ عَنْ ذِكْرِي﴾ i.e. the Quran, so they are blind and are not guided by it ﴿وَكَانُوا لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَمْعًا﴾ i.e. they were unable to hear from the Prophet what he recited to them, out of hatred for him, so they did not believe in it.

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿أَفَحَسِبَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا عِبَادِي﴾ i.e. My angels, Jesus and ʿUzayr ﴿مِنْ دُونِي أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ lords; the second object of يَتَّخِذُوا, while the second object of حَسِبَ is omitted. The meaning: did they think that the aforementioned taking would not anger Me and that I would not punish them for it? No indeed! ﴿إِنَّا أَعْتَدْنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ these and others ﴿نُزُلًا﴾ i.e. it is prepared for them like the lodging prepared for a guest.

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿قُلْ هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِالْأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَالًا﴾ a tamyīz (specification) agreeing with what it specifies; and He made them clear by His saying:

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ their work became void ﴿وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ﴾ think ﴿أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا﴾ a work for which they will be rewarded.

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ the proofs of His oneness, from the Quran and elsewhere ﴿وَلِقَائِهِ﴾ i.e. and in the resurrection, the reckoning, the reward and the punishment ﴿فَحَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ﴾ became void ﴿فَلَا نُقِيمُ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ وَزْنًا﴾ i.e. We do not assign them any worth.

celaleyn:106-106.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the matter that has been mentioned concerning the voiding of their works and other things; mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿جَزَاؤُهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ بِمَا كَفَرُوا وَاتَّخَذُوا آيَاتِي وَرُسُلِي هُزُوًا﴾ i.e. objects of mockery.

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ كَانَتْ لَهُمْ﴾ in Allah's knowledge ﴿جَنَّاتُ الْفِرْدَوْسِ﴾ it is the middle of Paradise and its highest part, and the annexation to it is explicative ﴿نُزُلًا﴾ a lodging.

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا لَا يَبْغُونَ﴾ they seek ﴿عَنْهَا حِوَلًا﴾ a move to anything else.

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿قُلْ لَوْ كَانَ الْبَحْرُ﴾ i.e. its water ﴿مِدَادًا﴾ it is what one writes with ﴿لِكَلِمَاتِ رَبِّي﴾ which indicate His wisdom and wonders, such that they were written with it ﴿لَنَفِدَ الْبَحْرُ﴾ in writing them ﴿قَبْلَ أَنْ تَنْفَدَ﴾ with tāʾ and yāʾ [يَنْفَدَ]: be exhausted ﴿كَلِمَاتُ رَبِّي وَلَوْ جِئْنَا بِمِثْلِهِ﴾ i.e. the sea ﴿مَدَدًا﴾ as an addition to it, it would be exhausted while they would not be finished; it is accusative as a tamyīz (specification).

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَنَا بَشَرٌ﴾ a human ﴿مِثْلُكُمْ يُوحَى إِلَيَّ أَنَّمَا إِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ﴾ أَنَّ, restrained by مَا, keeps its maṣdar-forming function; the meaning is: the oneness of God is revealed to me ﴿فَمَنْ كَانَ يَرْجُوا﴾ hopes for ﴿لِقَاءَ رَبِّهِ﴾ through resurrection and recompense ﴿فَلْيَعْمَلْ عَمَلًا صَالِحًا وَلَا يُشْرِكْ بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِ﴾ i.e. in it, by showing off ﴿أَحَدًا﴾
